newsitem.title: GERMANY: German president sees Spain in European currency.
newsitem.headline: German president sees Spain in European currency.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog said on Wednesday he was convinced that both Germany and Spain would be members of Europe's planned single currency.

According to the text of a speech for an evening banquet in honour of visiting Spanish King Juan Carlos, Herzog said: "The common currency will come and I am convinced that both our countries will be there."
Herzog, a member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, has a largely ceremonial role as head of state but sometimes speaks on political issues.
Earlier this month he cautioned against delaying the currency union, which is scheduled to begin in 1999.
Germans have been wary of admitting countries with traditionally weak currencies such as Spain and Italy into the first wave of economic and monetary union.
